item.title: Ellington, Rakiraki families seek action over decades of water shortages worsened by El Niño
item.description: Residents of Ellington Settlement in Rakiraki are calling for urgent action to address water shortages that they say have affected them for more than 30 years, as the river they rely on is now drying up due to the effects of El Niño. item.content:encoded:
Residents of Ellington Settlement in Rakiraki are calling for urgent action to address water shortages that they say have affected them for more than 30 years, as the river they rely on is now drying up due to the effects of El Niño.

Speaking to fijivillage News, a resident says more than 20 families depend on the river for their water supply, but falling water levels have left families without water for days at a time, affecting their ability to carry out daily household chores.

He says the river is also their source of drinking water, however it is usually contaminated by dirt, bacteria, dead plants and animals, as well as animal urine and waste.

The resident says there have even been instances when animal fur from a dead animal was found in the water.

He expresses frustration that the Water Authority of Fiji has not responded to their concerns despite numerous attempts to contact the authority by phone and email.

He says residents have to walk approximately 3 to 4 kilometres to reach the river and repair the pipes themselves whenever they are damaged or washed away by heavy rain or flooding to restore their water supply.

The residents are calling on the Government to provide a borehole.

They are also requesting that the Water Authority of Fiji consider extending the water pipes from the Duadua and Wananavu Resort junction to their community.

The resident says the distance to the Rarapatu area is only a few kilometres, and this extension would make a significant difference to the health and well-being of residents .

fijivillage News had earlier sent questions to the Water Authority of Fiji seeking an update on what is being done to address the issue and whether there are plans to extend the water network from the Rarapatu area towards Ellington Settlement, but no response was received.

We have also sent questions to the Ministry of Lands.

item.title: Uciwai residents in Nadi receive water after more than two weeks of disruption
item.description: Residents of Uciwai Village in Nadi have received water following a disruption that left families struggling without a continuous supply for more than two weeks. Uciwai Advisory Council representative Mahendra Reddy confirms that two water trucks visited the community this morning, with residents now receiving water.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Uciwai Village in Nadi have received water following a disruption that left families struggling without a continuous supply for more than two weeks.

Uciwai Advisory Council representative Mahendra Reddy confirms that two water trucks visited the community this morning, with residents now receiving water.

The update comes after residents raised concerns about the prolonged water shortage, which has affected households as children prepare for external examinations and families get ready for Diwali.

A resident, who requested anonymity, said the community had been experiencing water problems since last year, with the latest disruption leaving families struggling to store enough water for their daily needs.

The resident said there was no alternative water source available and appealed for urgent assistance.

Reddy says Nadi Depot had previously worked closely with the community by increasing water pressure at night, allowing residents to fill their containers and store water until the next supply.

However, he said the arrangement had recently stopped working, prompting residents to seek his assistance.

Reddy also said he had been informed that a pipe was being switched, which he understood would help restore the supply.

The Water Authority of Fiji says Uciwai is an intermittent supply area, with residents supplemented through water carting.

We have sent further questions on when a more reliable water supply can be expected.

item.title: Breast cancer survivor Bogi urges Fijians to get screened after early diagnosis
item.description: 59-year-old breast cancer survivor Mere Bogi is encouraging Fijians to undergo regular screenings after early detection helped save her life. Bogi shared this during the handover of a $10,000 donation from Merchant Finance staff to the Fiji Cancer Society through the company's Pinktober fundraising campaign.
item.content:encoded:
59-year-old breast cancer survivor Mere Bogi is encouraging Fijians to undergo regular screenings after early detection helped save her life.

Bogi shared this during the handover of a $10,000 donation from Merchant Finance staff to the Fiji Cancer Society through the company's Pinktober fundraising campaign.

She says her breast cancer was detected after she attended a Fiji Cancer Society outreach programme last year, where she was encouraged to undergo further testing.

Bogi says she was referred for a scan, which led to the early detection of her cancer and enabled her to receive treatment, including surgery.

Bogi says early detection made a difference in her journey and is urging people to take their health seriously

Fiji Cancer Society Chief Executive Officer Belinda Chan says awareness, regular screening, HPV vaccination and early detection are critical in improving cancer outcomes and saving lives.

Chan says while breast cancer remains one of the most common cancers affecting women, cervical cancer is also having an impact in Fiji.

She says support from organisations such as Merchant Finance helps the Society continue educating communities and supporting people affected by cancer.

Merchant Finance General Manager Central Mitesh Kumar says the donation reflects the generosity and collective effort of staff who supported the Pinktober campaign.

Kumar thanked employees for their contributions and says the company is proud to support the Fiji Cancer Society's work in raising awareness and assisting those affected by cancer.

The $10,000 donation was officially handed over at Merchant Finance's head office at FHL Tower this morning.
